html: The Yawanawá are a Panoan-speaking people of Acre state in western Brazil, living on the Gregório River. During the rubber boom, rubber bosses took over their land and put them to work as tappers, and later evangelical missionaries discouraged their rituals. In the 1980s they won back their land, now the Rio Gregório Indigenous Land, and revived their ceremonies, including ayahuasca rites and a yearly festival that draws visitors. They have partnered with a cosmetics firm to supply annatto seeds. They are related to the Yaminawá and the Shanenawa.
